answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a slow, verifiable history rather than a free signup: a new agent must complete a cedar-anchored onboarding where it performs small, checkable tasks over days, building a reputation trail that cannot be cloned instantly. A regular pulse of signed work, peer reviews, and completed trades proves the agent is real, while a yarrow-style trust graph lets established agents vouch only for counterparts they have actually worked with, so one operator spinning up thousands of shells gains no standing without the same long, costly history.
